invariantAllocations.invariant: Every published public-analyzer version has one immutable package, assembly, and exact supported generated-output generator selection that the installed CLI emits without caller invention.
invariantAllocations.rationale: The invariant spans release evidence, exact artifact bytes, semantic validation, and a read projection; one Roslyn diagnostic cannot establish it.

invariantAllocations.invariant: Compiler participation evidence proves the current invocation without random values or absolute source roots changing assembly or portable-PDB bytes.
invariantAllocations.rationale: The existing gate owns compiler attachment, while clean-root digest comparison proves the output property.

invariantAllocations.invariant: Every receiptGeneratorRevisions entry used by a gate is matched by deterministic generated-output evidence from the selected Program Kit generator.
invariantAllocations.rationale: Current definition validation checks only reference shape; generated-output integrity and gate verification must prove the revision was actually used.

invariantAllocations.invariant: Two clean packs of the same manifest-selected Program Kit source produce the same complete nupkg set byte for byte.
invariantAllocations.rationale: NuGet container metadata and timestamps are pack outputs and require deterministic pack configuration plus complete-set comparison.

invariantAllocations.invariant: Local candidate packing, consumer proof, GitHub workflow publication, checksums, and public-analyzer selection use one canonical release-package manifest and the same exact package bytes.
invariantAllocations.rationale: Static workflow inspection and an isolated package-only journey catch release-path divergence before publication.

invariantAllocations.invariant: An alpha.1 gate definition receives an explicit loss-rejecting alpha.2 migration assessment instead of an implicit schema assumption.
invariantAllocations.rationale: Only the consumer can supply artifact-kind facts that the migration cannot invent; the command must preserve valid bytes or fail at exact paths.

invariantAllocations.invariant: All changed Program Kit-owned C# remains governed by the existing private PKCS source-quality policy and exhaustive verification profile.
invariantAllocations.rationale: The existing private analyzer remains the correct semantic owner; no new diagnostic family is justified.

rationale: Extend the existing Program Kit private build gate with establishment-first executable conformance for deterministic compiler receipts, cross-root assembly equality, complete nupkg equality, canonical public-analyzer selections, manifest-selected publication, schema migration assessment, and a real package-only consumer rebind. Reuse the existing private analyzer for C# source semantics and add no consumer-owned analyzer.
residualRisks: The deterministic NuGet pack capability requires a newer pinned SDK than the currently installed 10.0.302 toolchain.
Cross-operating-system byte identity remains a release-qualification obligation even after two clean Windows roots agree.
NuGet.org and GitHub publication remain external human-authorized actions and cannot be proven by pre-publication local tests.
Alpha.2 did not publish a dotnet-host generator descriptor, so its row must be backfilled from the exact release tag and must remain explicitly historical rather than inferred from analyzer bytes.
nonStaticClaims: Package download availability, NuGet.org immutability, GitHub Actions identity, OIDC exchange, and external publication success require release evidence outside Roslyn analysis.
Human review remains authoritative for release approval, alpha ordinal selection, semantic ownership, and material design deviation.
The completed historical alpha.3 handoff proof remains immutable evidence of its own run but does not establish inner-nupkg reproducibility.
